corrected_equation_text:
The meta-feature vector phi in ?^32 is constructed as:

  phi = [phi_CWRU, phi_Ind, phi_NASA, phi_Curr, phi_Therm, mu_p, sigma^2_p, H_g]

where for each expert e in {CWRU, Induction, NASA, Current, Thermal}:
  phi_e = [p_e^(0), p_e^(1), p_e^(2), H(p_e), m_e]  in ?^5
  p_e^(k): softmax probability for class k in {Normal, Warning, Critical}
  H(p_e) = -Sigma_k p_e^(k) ln(p_e^(k)):  Shannon entropy (uncertainty)
  m_e = p_e^(argmax) - p_e^(2nd argmax):  decision margin

Global statistics (7 additional dimensions):
  mu_p = (1/5) Sigma_e p_e  in ?^3:  mean class probability across experts
  sigma^2_p = Var_e(p_e)    in ?^3:  expert disagreement per class
  H_g = H(mu_p)         in ?^1:  global entropy of the consensus distribution

Dimension count: 5 experts x 5 = 25, plus 3 + 3 + 1 = 7 global = 32 total. OK
reviewer_response: Reviewer ?III.C notes: 'the remaining 7 dimensions of sigma are unspecified.' These 7 dimensions ARE specified in the code (src/features/meta_fusion_features.py, extract_meta_features_from_predictions()): mean_p (3 dims, mu_p), var_p (3 dims, sigma^2_p), global_ent (1 dim, H_g). The paper's Eq. (5) needs to be expanded to show all three components. The reviewer's count of 25 is correct for the expert blocks; the remaining 7 are the global cross-expert statistics appended in the same function.
